key_insight: ArogyaSutra combines a multilingual medical dataset with a multi-agent reasoning framework to improve multimodal healthcare question answering across Indian languages.
clinical_relevance: The work could help make AI-assisted medical information more accessible for patients and clinicians in low-resource, Indic-language settings.
method: Built ArogyaBodha, a large multilingual multimodal medical QA dataset from 8 sources.
Covers 31 body systems, 6 imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains across English and 7 Indian languages.
Proposed ArogyaSutra, an actor-critic multi-agent system with tool grounding, dual memory, and trajectory distillation.
evidence_signal: Experiments reported improved multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablations supporting each major component.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown in experimental settings, but real-world clinical use still needs careful validation for safety, robustness, and workflow integration.
paper_title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
